segments.name: Muscle-conscious active GLP-1 users
segments.description: People on Mounjaro/Zepbound/Wegovy who already work out (gym, Peloton, running) and are alarmed that their lifts, stamina and lean mass are dropping along with the fat.

values.value: previously active adult returning to training
own gym routine with no structured logging
smart scale or DEXA scans to watch lean mass
bodyweight workouts a few times a week
problem-aware, actively looking for a fix

needs: Keep strength and lean mass while losing fat
Hit protein targets despite having no appetite
Track lifts and performance, not just pounds lost
Know whether weakness is the drug, the deficit or the training
barriers: Low energy and fatigue make workouts feel pointless
Never hungry, so eating enough is hard
Already juggling a gym habit and DIY supplements; unsure an app adds anything

segments.name: New starters figuring out GLP-1 nutrition
segments.description: People in their first months on Zepbound or semaglutide who suddenly need to eat enough protein, fiber and water rather than eat less, and feel left alone to work it out.

values.value: working adult / parent newly prescribed a GLP-1
long-time dieter with WW or calorie-counting history
GLP-1 tracker app (MeAgain, Shotsy) with food log

needs: Guidance on eating enough protein, fiber and water on a suppressed appetite
A non-shaming approach that isn't about restriction
Avoid side effects like muscle loss and saggy skin
barriers: Past diet apps (WW, calorie countdowns) hurt their mental health
Logging feels like a full-time job
Not referred to a nutritionist; don't know what good looks like
Wary of paywalls and nagging notifications

segments.name: Data-driven self-trackers
segments.description: Organized, numbers-minded GLP-1 users who log doses, side effects, weight and macros, often out of pocket, and want one place to see patterns and show their doctor.

values.value: several separate apps (food, hydration, smart scale)
using a competitor, open to switching

needs: All data in one place instead of separate apps
Charts that reveal plateaus and side-effect patterns
Reports to share with their doctor
Integrations with Apple Health, scales and food loggers
barriers: Subscription fatigue after a short trial
Switching cost from existing logs and saved meals
Already loyal to an established GLP-1 tracker

segments.name: Maintainers and tapering users
segments.description: People who have reached or are near goal and are tapering or stopping the medication, and fear returning hunger and weight regain.

values.value: user stopping for cost or side effects
tapering dose with or without doctor guidance

needs: Habits and structure that hold once appetite returns
Calm, non-obsessive way to monitor progress
Keep the body they built (muscle, strength) long term
barriers: Belief that willpower alone won't be enough
Spending fatigue after paying for medication
Unsure an app can replace the shot's appetite control

lexicon.quote: Still working out 5x a week but my lifts have stalled. I'm not getting stronger.
Gym routine hasn’t changed, but I’m shrinking and weaker. Maybe need more protein?
I’ve lost 50 lbs, but the last DEXA scan showed I’ve dropped lean mass too. Not thrilled about that.
My arms are looking deflated. The fat is gone but so is the definition I worked for.
You gotta strength train and eat enough. Easier said than done when you're never hungry.
Tracking strength now instead of just pounds lost. Helps me feel like I’m still progressing.
Upped my protein and added creatine. Not sure it fixed everything, but it helped.
I had to force myself back into weight training. Felt pointless at first, but now I feel more stable.
I used to be strong. Now I can’t even carry groceries without getting winded. It’s scary.
I have one of those smart scales and it's showing muscle mass down. Clothes fit weird - like I’m shrinking.
I look better in clothes, but I feel worse in my body. I don’t feel strong anymore.
I don’t lift heavy anymore, but bodyweight workouts 3x/week made a difference.
i needed help making sure I ate enough and enough of the right stuff.
You’re just left on your own to figure out your nutrition.
For me, I find it feels like a full time job and definitely struggle to get my nutrients.
I think it’s SO unhealthy and negligent that people aren’t automatically referred to a nutritionist to help safety manage health when using GLP-1s.
I log almost every day just to make sure at a very minimum my protein intake & water is reached.
Hard to tell if it’s the drug or the fact I’m eating 800 calories a day without trying.
It’s probably just the calorie deficit. I'm barely eating because I never feel hungry.
I had done WW previously and that was so bad for my mental health because the points were a "countdown" to me
When I started, the most common post-GLP 1 side effect I read about was saggy skin.
It doesn’t focus on calories or fat shaming- the protein and the fiber are definitely running the show
In the beginning I tried to use notebooks, spreadsheets, even a wall calendar, to log everything. I couldn’t keep up.
But as soon as I saw that after a one week trial I would have to pay, I had my usual reaction - nope.
With what I’m paying out of pocket for Zepbound, the cost is a minimal addition that is making my life much easier!
I’m a very data driven person and when someone told me about this app, I downloaded it immediately.
With this app I can clearly see when I’m plateaued and when it might make sense to talk to the doctor about increasing my dosage.
I used a spreadsheet I found online to track in the beginning but I switched to shotsy when it was available.
Unlike the barebones app from my semaglutide provider (which only tracks weight and doses), this one is incredibly useful.
I’m so grateful the main features aren’t locked behind a paywall like most other apps have them
I also wanted to add how grateful I am that privacy is taken seriously, no tracking, no nonsense, no data harvesting
I use the baritastic app for logging my food (just because I have a bunch of meals and foods already saved there from before)
It puts all the information I had in separate apps into one convenient place.
I should feel proud, but instead I feel scared and exposed.
Within two weeks of stopping, my hunger was back like it had never left.
I’m weighing myself daily and over-analyzing every meal. I hate that I feel this way again.
I can’t relax. Every time the scale goes up a pound, I panic.
I gained back 25 lbs in 3 months. I wasn’t mentally ready to be off it.
I kept telling myself I could maintain it. I couldn’t. I’m back on 5mg now.
It was heartbreaking to watch the number climb again. But it taught me that this is lifelong.
I tapered from 10 to 5 to 2.5 before stopping. Took it slow, and it helped.
Now, I’m slowly titrating down to that range as I begin maintenance.
I am in maintenance now, but I really still love this app.
